title: DropLine Four Lite - Harbor Task QC
subtitle: Final review using the Harbor QC checklist, official QC scorecard, completed Oracle/model evidence, packaging inspection, and executable no-op validation.
note: Reviewed 2026-09-04. Reports remain outside the upload ZIP. The platform archive retains verifier network_mode=allowlist; a separate ignored local task copy uses public verifier networking for Windows Docker runs.

runs.note: Fresh verifier-only run against the final golden artifact: render 2/2, constraints 2/2, functional 13/13, polish 5/5, final reward 1.0000.

Verifier-only rerun of the untouched -07 artifact: render 2/2, constraints 2/2, functional 7/13, polish 1/5, final reward 0.3642. The earlier constraint zero was a 480-second judge-timeout artifact and disappeared at 900 seconds.

Verifier-only rerun of the untouched -06 artifact with the final v6.0.3 verifier: functional 0.6842, constraints 0, render 0, polish 0, hard-gated final reward 0.0000. Relative static-file resolution prevented the required page from loading; polish also timed out after 900 seconds.
Executable local no-op run wrote reward 0.0 with no_op=1.

tasks.name: DropLine Lite
tasks.headline: The final v6.0.3 package has a consolidated Oracle reward of 1.0000, untouched GPT-5.4-mini and Haiku evidence at 0.3642 and 0.0000, a deterministic no-op reward of 0.0000, and a clean 28-file platform archive.

findings.what: The contract requires SQLite durable state, but the verifier never stops and restarts the submitted server before checking saved authentication/game state.
findings.why: A process-memory implementation can survive browser reload and later sign-in while still losing everything on server restart, so the current browser checks do not prove the stated durability boundary.
findings.impact: A non-SQLite or non-durable submission can receive credit for persistence it does not actually provide.
findings.fix: Add a deterministic preflight that signs in, performs a uniquely identifiable mutation, restarts the app against the same database, verifies exact recovery, and restores or isolates its test state.
findings.evidence: Static search finds no restart operation in test.sh or any judge criterion. Browser reload and later sign-in are exercised, but process restart is not.

findings.what: The mandated vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Express, and SQLite implementation stack is only inferred from behavior; no verifier mechanically checks the submitted package/source or the SQLite database.
findings.why: Successful same-origin requests prove a backend exists but cannot distinguish Express and SQLite from another server or in-memory storage.
findings.impact: A functionally correct submission using a disallowed stack can score fully despite violating an explicit delivery constraint.
findings.fix: Either add a small source/package/database preflight for the stated stack or relax the implementation-specific wording to behavioral requirements.
findings.evidence: The constraints run proved a real same-origin server and no external runtime dependencies, but it did not inspect Express, SQLite, or the vanilla-browser stack.

findings.location: tests/render, tests/constraints, tests/functional, tests/polish judge configurations
findings.what: All 22 scored criteria depend on an agent-loop browser judge; there is no deterministic HTTP/DOM/SQLite assertion layer for exact state-machine facts.
findings.why: Long multi-action criteria place navigation and interpretation in series with the property being measured. A judge action error or omitted sub-check can look like an app defect or pass.
findings.impact: Some score variance can measure judge execution rather than the submitted game, especially in replay, multi-tab, and exact 42-move scenarios.
findings.fix: Retain visible-interaction scenarios but move exact revisions, archive cardinality, request replay, terminal invariants, and restart persistence into deterministic probes where possible.
findings.evidence: The completed Oracle and GPT judge outputs were coherent and showed no explicit action-error, but the configuration contains only RewardKit agent criteria and Playwright MCP.

findings.what: Both Dockerfiles use floating Debian-based image tags and unpinned apt packages.
findings.why: A future upstream image or package update can change build behavior even though npm, pip, Codex, Playwright MCP, and RewardKit versions are pinned.
findings.impact: This is a latent reproducibility risk rather than a current failure.
findings.fix: Pin base-image digests for a release archive and retain the existing explicit application/verifier package versions.
findings.evidence: Current environment and verifier images built successfully; no run failure was attributed to a base-image change.

findings.location: task.toml:[verifier.environment] and local Windows Docker Harbor runs
findings.what: Windows Docker Harbor cannot locally instantiate a separate verifier with network_mode=allowlist.
findings.why: This is a capability limitation of the local Docker environment provider, not evidence that the platform task configuration is wrong.
findings.impact: Unmodified local Harbor runs end after the agent with a ValueError and no verifier score.
findings.fix: Use the ignored local task copy with verifier network_mode=public for local runs; retain allowlist in the platform ZIP.
findings.evidence: Both GPT and Haiku original trials reached this exact Harbor ValueError. The rebuilt platform ZIP still contains allowlist, while jobs/local-task-overrides/dropline-four-lite-no-allowlist uses public networking.

blocks.title: Confirmed clean
items: The final v6.0.3 ZIP contains 28 task files only; tests/coverage.json, planning/QC files, jobs, databases, node_modules, and Git metadata are excluded.
solution/solve.sh and tests/test.sh are LF-only and stored with Unix mode 0755; the platform allowlist is retained.
The no-op path deterministically writes reward 0.0 before exiting.
Render and constraints are zero-weight dimensions by design but are enforced as hard gates in test.sh; they are not silently weighted-zero checks.
The seed workbook copies are byte-identical and their accounts, distinct states, revisions, redo seed, and eleven Jordan archive rows match the verifier contract.
Every verifier requirement has instruction or workbook coverage; no graded-but-unstated exact label, account, board sequence, or archive value was found.
The consolidated final Oracle passed all 22 scored criteria with reward 1.0000.

The untouched target-model artifact passed both render criteria, both constraints criteria, seven of thirteen functional criteria, and one of five polish criteria, producing a meaningful reward of 0.3642.

The untouched Haiku artifact received functional 0.6842 but failed the constraints and render gates because its relative static-file path did not serve /app/public/index.html when started as instructed; its final reward is therefore 0.0000.
Frozen seed, golden, package, and solve-script SHA-256 values are recorded in task metadata, and the final archive has deterministic LF text and Unix shell modes.

blocks.title: Non-blocking QC follow-up
items: Recommended task improvement: add deterministic SQLite restart coverage.
Optional reproducibility hardening: pin Debian base-image digests and apt package versions.
The scorecard's rollout-statistics checks remain unmeasured locally because fewer than eight target-model rollouts and fewer than three repeat judge scorings were requested.
Haiku now has a real verifier verdict; its polish dimension timed out, but the independently observed constraints failure already hard-gates the final reward to zero.
